source.title: Recovering Plasticity of Neural Networks via Soft Weight Rescaling
source.authors: Seungwon Oh; Sangyeon Park; Isaac Han; Kyung-Joong Kim

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own standard image-classification test-accuracy results for explicit weight regularization methods, using a different intervention and measure from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports accuracy results for soft weight rescaling (SWR), L2 regularization, and L2 Init. These test generalization under explicit regularization, but do not test the specific interventions or measures named by V1–V8. Cited findings and figure-only warm-start and continual-learning curves are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests weight rescaling, weight regularization, and plasticity recovery. Its own results do not test any of V1–V8. Generalization accuracy alone does not establish the specific comparisons those versions name.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but incomplete: the authors conclude that SWR bounds weight growth, improves layer balancedness, and helps plasticity and classification performance across stationary, warm-start, and continual-learning settings. They also acknowledge that L2 sometimes performs better and that learning-rate decay requires further investigation.
record.recipe_differences: Tests soft weight rescaling and other weight regularizers on image classification; it does not reproduce the interventions or measurements in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ across datasets and models; with learning-rate decay, SWR+re-init generally outperforms standalone SWR, with a slight drop for VGG-16.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 shows higher mean test accuracy with SWR than vanilla training in all five dataset/model combinations. With learning-rate decay, Table 5 shows higher mean accuracy in four of five combinations, rather than the record's three: only MNIST is lower (0.9796 versus 0.9798). These mean differences are not established as statistically significant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Soft weight rescaling can improve image-classification test accuracy, with benefits depending on architecture, dataset, and learning-rate schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Warm-start and continual-learning experiments compare SWR with vanilla training, regularization, and re-initialization methods. The authors report improved plasticity and fewer immediate accuracy drops from rescaling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight rescaling can mitigate plasticity loss when training data becomes available incrementally.

record.problems: The paper reports test accuracy rather than train–test gaps. It gives no uncertainty tests or significance estimates; results are averaged over five seeds, except three seeds for VGG-16.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows were omitted. Warm-start and continual-learning results are shown in figures, but they concern changing-data training settings rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep or measurement beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No matched convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention; the principal MLP and CNN results use different datasets.
Adam is used throughout; no empirical comparison with SGD or momentum SGD.
Batch size is fixed at 256; no batch-size comparison.
No dropout comparison. VGG-16 is configured without dropout, but dropout removal is not tested.
No magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, ranking of generalization gaps, or comparison with alternative generalization measures. Weight norms and layer balancedness measure different properties.
No identification or removal of memorized examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification is inconsistent with its correct assessment that none of V1–V8 is tested. Tables 1 and 5 report uncertainty alongside means, although the paper provides no significance tests. Its broad claims of consistent superiority should be read alongside the mixed method rankings in those tables.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label versus random-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with other generalization measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
